column1: # Cases where fizh and bergamot-translator disagree, with the diagnosis.
# These are NOT recorded as golden output, because a golden file that encodes
# wrong output reads a future fix as a regression. Each row carries what fizh
# produces, what bergamot produces, and why they differ. `tools/regress.py`:
#   * fizh still produces its column      -> pass, still diverging
#   * fizh now produces bergamot's column -> pass, reported RESOLVED, re-record
#   * fizh produces a third thing         -> FAIL, something else moved
# source <TAB> fizh <TAB> bergamot <TAB> diagnosis
# -- Currently empty, and the reason is worth keeping --------------------------
# The one row this file ever held was `La reunión se ha aplazado hasta el
# jueves.`, where fizh opened with "of the meeting" against bergamot's "The
# meeting". It was diagnosed here as an irreducible step-0 near-tie: logits
# The=9.6698 of=9.6161, a margin of 0.054 against the ~0.26 int8 quantization
# noise floor of ADR 0007. The diagnosis was wrong, and wrong in a way this
# file is built to make expensive.
# The margin was real. The conclusion drawn from it was not. A 0.054 gap says
# the two candidates are close *in fizh's logits*; it says nothing about
# whether fizh's logits are the ones bergamot computes. They were not: fizh
# seeded the decoder with `emb(</s>)` where Marian zero-fills (ADR 0015), so
# every first token was decided from the wrong decoder input. The row resolved
# for cause, not by coincidence.
# The lesson, recorded because the next near-tie will look identical: a small
# margin measured on your own logits is not evidence of a near-tie in the
# reference. It is evidence that *your* two candidates are close. Before
# calling a divergence irreducible, check the position — this one sat at token
# 0 on 42% of segments, and no rounding artifact is that punctual.
